title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building the combinatorial skeleton of the boundary ('structure à l'infini') of the moduli stacks M_{g,ν} of stable ν-pointed curves. Strata are indexed by 'm-graphes': dual graphs with genus-weighted vertices S(G), edges A(G) and marked legs. On the previous page he defined 'morphismes de normalisation' between m-graphes and their strict version. He showed that strict ones form a category whose morphisms are monomorphisms, and that strict sub-objects of G correspond to subsets C ⊂ A(G).

This page:
(1) Given C ⊂ A(G), the 'découpe' of G along C cuts each edge of C at its midpoint. Equivalently, those edges are removed and each is replaced by a pair of new marked points (legs). This is the graph-theoretic shadow of partially normalizing the nodes indexed by C.
(2) For a normalisation morphism G' → G (130): if it is strict, G' is stable iff G is. Stability means 2g(v)−2+n(v)>0 at each vertex. Cutting edges does not change vertex genera or valences, since half-edges become legs. In the general case, if the vertex map S' → S is surjective and G' is stable, then G is stable.
(3) Let X/S be a 'courbe spéciale' over an arbitrary base S that is 'épinglée par G', i.e. a stable curve with a rigidification identifying its degeneration (dual-graph) type with G. As at the start of the section, one canonically attaches to X a G'-pinned special curve, namely the partial normalization along the nodes cut. This gives a functor (131) M_G(S) → M_{G'}(S).

The next page concludes:
- the functor is compatible with base change, giving morphisms of modular multiplicities (stacks) M_G → M_{G'};
- G ↦ M_G is contravariant and functorial for normalisation morphisms of stable m-graphs;
- strict normalisations give isomorphisms;
- M of a disjoint sum of graphs is the product of the M_{G_α}.

In modern terms this is the identification of a pinned boundary stratum with a product of moduli stacks attached to the vertices, M_Γ^{rigidified} ≅ ∏_v M_{g(v),n(v)}, via partial normalization (the inverse of Knudsen clutching). It is organized as a contravariant functor on a category of stable graphs with cutting/normalisation morphisms.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The stability claims are correct under the natural reading: strict means bijective on vertices with edges turned into pairs of legs, so local valences and genera are preserved.
Gap: the general-case claim (S'→S surjective, G' stable ⇒ G stable) depends on the precise definition of non-strict normalisation morphisms on the previous page and is only asserted ('on voit').

Gap: the canonical construction of the G'-pinned curve over an arbitrary base is referred back to the start of the section, not redone. It needs the nodes in C to be étale-locally trivially labelled, which is what the pinning provides.

ideas.what: Cutting ('découpe') a dual graph along a set C of edges, replacing each cut edge by two marked legs
ideas.modern_name: Edge-cutting / partial normalization of stable graphs; the inverse of clutching (grafting) in modular operads
ideas.usually_credited_to: Knudsen (clutching morphisms, 1983); Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998); Behrend–Manin (category of stable modular graphs, 1996-97)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme speaks of 'découpage' of surfaces/curves and the boundary strata of the Teichmüller tower, but not this formal graph calculus

ideas.what: Stability of a graph is preserved and reflected by strict normalisation morphisms
ideas.modern_name: Stable modular graphs closed under cutting edges

ideas.what: Functor M_G(S) → M_{G'}(S) sending a G-pinned special curve to its partial normalization, compatible with base change, making G ↦ M_G a contravariant functor (stacks) on stable m-graphs
ideas.modern_name: Gluing/normalization maps between boundary strata ∏_v M̄_{g(v),n(v)} → ∂M̄_{g,n}; moduli stacks as a (contravariant) functor on the graph category / modular operad structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Knudsen 1983; Getzler–Kapranov 1998; Behrend 1997 (Gromov-Witten stacks via graph categories)
ideas.where_published: Only the general philosophy of the 'tour de Teichmüller' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a category of stable 'm-graphes' with (strict) normalisation morphisms and a contravariant functor G ↦ M_G to moduli multiplicities (stacks). Strict morphisms give isomorphisms and disjoint sums go to products. This is essentially the modular-operad / graph-category formalism of the boundary of M̄_{g,n}, predating Getzler–Kapranov and Behrend–Manin. It is a modest historical anticipation, not a new result.
missed.quote: on lui associe canoniquement une courbe spéciale G'-épinglée, d'où un foncteur (131) M_G(S) → M_{G'}(S)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit only: it documents that the functorial graph-indexed description of boundary strata (used in modular operads and Gromov–Witten theory) was part of Grothendieck's Teichmüller-tower program. The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the standard description of boundary strata via partial normalization and stable graphs, in Grothendieck's own idiosyncratic language ('épinglée', 'multiplicités modulaires'). Mildly interesting as an early functorial graph-category formulation, but specialists would recognize it as Knudsen / Getzler–Kapranov material.
transcription_corrections: 'Soit un morphisme de numérotations entre graphes' should read 'Soit un morphisme de normalisation entre m-graphes'.
'Si c'est un morphisme de numérotations strict' should read 'Si c'est un morphisme de normalisation strict'.

'(ce qui revient à "contracter" les arêtes' is more likely '(ce qui revient à "enlever" les arêtes, et à remplacer les arêtes correspondantes par des pts marqués)'. This means cutting, not contracting.

'dans ce cas (comme précédemment[?] comme au début de la section) qu'on lui associe' should read 'on voit (comme au début de la section) qu'on lui associe canoniquement...'. 'comme précédemment' appears to be struck/replaced.
In (131) the source M_G may carry a decoration on G (possibly G̃); the target is M_{G'}(S).
In the general-case parenthesis, S', S denote vertex sets of the m-graphes, not base schemes.
